content:
# 1 Enoch Chapter 98 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 98:2 — Description of luxury ('poured out as water' / 'lavished like water')

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "they-shall-be-poured-out-as-water" | Literal Ge'ez |
| LOGOS | "shall you be lavished like water" | 'Lavished' captures the extravagance |
| PNEUMA | "drowning in luxury and feasting" | Paraphrase; 'drowning' is vivid but not present |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS 'lavished like water.' Both EMET and LOGOS preserve the water metaphor. PNEUMA's 'drowning' is vivid but interpolated.

---

## 98:4 — Sin as human invention — theological crux

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "sin-has-not-been-sent-upon-the-earth, but-man-of-himself-has-created-it" | Literal; passive/active contrast preserved |
| LOGOS | "sin was not sent upon the earth — but man created it himself" | Formal; dash dramatizes the contrast |
| PNEUMA | "sin was never sent into the world as part of creation. Human beings invented it themselves." | Two sentences; 'invented' for 'created' |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. The passive/active contrast ("was not sent... created himself") is essential to the argument. LOGOS's dash preserves the rhetorical turn. PNEUMA's addition "as part of creation" is interpretive expansion.

---

## 98:5 — Barrenness verse

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "barrenness-has-not-been-given-to-the-woman" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "barrenness was not given to the woman" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "Barrenness was not placed in women by God" | 'By God' specifies agent; 'women' for 'the woman' |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. 'By God' (PNEUMA) adds an agent that the Ge'ez leaves implicit. 'The woman' (singular) preferred over PNEUMA's 'women' — the Ge'ez may be referring to a class or representative figure.

---

## 98:7 — 'think in your spirit' vs. 'tell yourself'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "think-not-in-your-spirit-nor-say-in-your-heart" | Literal; two distinct faculties |
| LOGOS | "Do not think in your spirit, nor say in your heart" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "Don't tell yourself you don't know this" | Collapses the two faculties |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. The Ge'ez distinguishes between internal thought (spirit) and internal speech (heart). This distinction — important in ancient anthropology — should be preserved.

---

## 98:9 — 'good hap' vs. 'good fortune'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "good-hap-shall-not-be-your-portion" | 'Good hap' = archaic English for good fortune/luck |
| LOGOS | "good fortune shall not be your portion" | Modern equivalent |
| PNEUMA | "wonder why good fortune never comes to you" | Paraphrase; adds 'wonder' |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. 'Good hap' (EMET) is archaic without adding precision. PNEUMA's addition of 'wonder' is not in the text.

---

## 98:11 — 'obstinate-of-heart' vs. 'stubborn of heart' vs. 'hardhearted'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "ye-obstinate-of-heart" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "you stubborn of heart" | Standard equivalent |
| PNEUMA | "hardhearted people" | Single adjective; loses the construct 'of heart' |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS 'stubborn of heart.' The construct form 'X of heart' is a Semitic idiom (cf. Ezekiel 3:7, hard of heart) that should be preserved. PNEUMA's single adjective loses the body metaphor.

---

**Total disagreements this chapter: 6**
